body:
From the harness discussion on task:30881953fb66677f (note 10). A model provider can skip re-reading the start of a prompt if it is exactly the same as the start of an earlier one (prompt caching). In a fresh run's brief, though, the agent reference (the largest fixed block) comes after the `session start` reply, which is different for every task: status, then the work context, then other projects, then the reference. So no two runs share that cached start.

### Change
- Put the fixed agent reference first in a fresh run's brief, and the task's own content after it. Then every run on the same endpoint reuses one cached prefix (the agent program's prompt, the tools, the reference).
- Check that nothing changing (time, ids, status counts) sits inside or before the reference.
- Show a cache-hit ratio per run on the board's token line (tokens read from cache ÷ all input tokens, summed over the run). The board already reports cached tokens.

### Acceptance
- Two fresh briefs for different tasks start with the same bytes for the whole reference.
- Resumed runs are unchanged.
- The token line shows the ratio when the agent program reports cached tokens, and leaves it out when it doesn't.

### Out of scope
The agent program's own system prompt (Solace doesn't control it), pinning a run to one llama.cpp server slot, and anything that needs a Solace-owned harness.
title: briefs: fixed reference first, for caching
